name: ServiceNow
description: Incidents, requests, knowledge articles and users in ServiceNow ITSM.

objects.label: incidents
objects.description: Records in the Incident table: something is broken or degraded.

fields.label: priority
fields.description: Calculated from impact and urgency; you cannot set it directly.

fields.label: category
fields.description: Values depend on the instance. Hardware, Software, Network and Inquiry are common.

fields.label: caller
fields.description: The person affected, not necessarily who reported it.

objects.label: requests
objects.description: Service catalog requests and the items requested in them.

fields.label: number
fields.description: A REQ number for the request or a RITM number for an item in it.

fields.label: catalog item
fields.description: What was ordered, like New laptop or VPN access.

objects.label: knowledge articles
objects.description: Articles in a knowledge base, published or not.

fields.label: valid until
fields.description: Articles past this date are hidden from the portal.

objects.label: users
objects.description: People in the User table: employees, contractors and their reporting lines.

fields.label: active
fields.description: False for people who have left or been locked out.

actions.label: an incident
actions.description: One new incident per record, opened for the caller you name.

params.label: with urgency
params.description: Priority is worked out from urgency and impact.

params.label: titled with
params.description: The field that becomes the short description.

actions.label: a note on each record
actions.description: Append to the incidents or requests in the source. Work notes stay internal; additional comments go to the caller.

actions.label: a state change
actions.description: Move the incidents in the source to another state. Resolving needs a resolution note; closing is left to the service desk.

guidance: ServiceNow is reached through the Table REST API on the company's own instance (yourcompany.service-now.com), normally as a dedicated integration user with basic auth or OAuth and roles limited to the tables the plan touches. Every write is audited under that user and business rules fire exactly as they do in the UI, so a state change can send notifications or start approvals. Never close or cancel records automatically; set them to Resolved at most and let the service desk close them.

setup.notes: Ask the ServiceNow platform owner for an integration user with read access to the tables the plan names and write access only where it creates or updates. Most companies have an intake form for this and want to see the plan first.
